lines.say: Here's the plan, in five parts.
lines.cap: Here's the plan, in [five] parts.
lines.heard: Here's the plan in five parts.

lines.say: One, the big map. Two, who does what. Three, three requests traced through it.

lines.say: Picture an airport. Check in, security, then the gate. One job each, before you board.
lines.cap: An airport: [check-in], [security], the [gate]. One [job] each.
lines.heard: Picture an airport, check in security than the gate. One job each before you board.

lines.say: A request travels the same way. A C D N may answer straight away. A gateway checks who you are. The app does the real work.
lines.cap: A [CDN] may answer. A [gateway] checks who you are. The [app] does the work.
lines.heard: A request travels the same way. A CDN may answer straight away. A gateway checks who you are. The app does the real work.

lines.say: Here is the whole map, straight from the handbook. It starts with a client: a browser, a mobile app, another service, even an AI agent.
lines.cap: The whole [map]. It starts with a [client]: browser, app, service, [AI agent].
lines.heard: Here is the whole map straight from the handbook. It starts with a client, a browser, a mobile app, another service, even an AI agent.

lines.say: The client reaches a C D N or load balancer, then an API gateway, then your application service.
lines.cap: [CDN], then [gateway], then your [application] service.
lines.heard: The client reaches a CDN or load balancer, then an API gateway, then your application service.

lines.say: And behind the application sit four things: a cache, a database, a message queue with workers, and an AI gateway that reaches the language model providers.
lines.cap: Behind the app: [cache], [database], [queue], [AI gateway].
lines.heard: And behind the application sit four things. A cache, a database, a message queue with workers, and an AI gateway that reaches the language model providers.

lines.say: The chapter draws the same system a second way, grouped into layers.
lines.cap: The same system, grouped into [layers].
lines.heard: The chapter draws the same system a second way, grouped into layers.

lines.say: Edge. Gateway. Application. Data. And AI.
lines.cap: [Edge]. [Gateway]. [Application]. [Data]. And [AI].
lines.heard: Edge Gateway, Application Data and AI.

lines.say: Five layers, each with a narrow job. Client, edge, gateway, application, then data and AI.
lines.cap: Each layer has a [narrow job]. Client, edge, gateway, application, [data and AI].
lines.heard: 5 layers each with a narrow job, client, edge, gateway application, then data and AI.

lines.say: The handbook's mental model is a company org chart, not one person doing everything.
lines.cap: A company [org chart], not one person doing [everything].
lines.heard: The handbook's mental model is a company org chart, not one person doing everything.

lines.say: The C D N is the receptionist. If they already have your answer, they hand it over right there.
lines.cap: The [CDN] is the receptionist: they hand over a [cached] answer.
lines.heard: The CDN is the receptionist. If they already have your answer, they hand it over right there.

lines.say: The gateway is security and routing. It checks your badge, then sends you to the right department.
lines.cap: The [gateway] checks your [badge], then [routes] you.
lines.heard: The gateway is security and routing. It checks your badge, then sends you to the right department.

lines.say: The application service is that department, doing the real work. The database is the filing cabinet.
lines.cap: The [app] does the work. The [database] is the filing cabinet.
lines.heard: The application service is that department doing the real work. The database is the filing cabinet.

lines.say: The queue is the ticket system. The AI gateway talks to outside AI vendors.
lines.cap: The [queue] is the ticket system. The [AI gateway] talks to outside vendors.
lines.heard: The Q is the ticket system. The AI Gateway talks to outside AI vendors.

lines.say: Zoom in on the gateway: one front door, one address for web, mobile and partner clients.
lines.cap: The [gateway]: one [front door], one address.
lines.heard: Zoom in on the gateway. One front door. One address for web, mobile and partner clients.

lines.say: It does the shared chores once: authenticate, rate limit, and route to the right private service.
lines.cap: [Authenticate], [rate limit], [route]. Once, for everyone.
lines.heard: It does the shared chores once. Authenticate rate limit and route to the right private service.

lines.say: Fail a check, and the request is rejected right there: a four zero one, or a four twenty nine. No service does any work.
lines.cap: Fail a check: [401] or [429]. No service does any work.
lines.heard: Fail a check and the request is rejected right there. A 401 or a 429. No service does any work.

lines.say: And it stays dumb. A gateway that also holds business logic stops being a gateway.
lines.cap: Keep it [dumb]. No [business logic] in the gateway.
lines.heard: And it stays dumb. A gateway that also holds business logic stops being a gateway.

lines.say: The cache sits beside the app. Reads check it first.
lines.cap: The [cache] sits beside the app. Reads check it [first].
lines.heard: The cache sits beside the app, reads check it first.

lines.say: A hit comes back in about one millisecond. A miss reads the database, then saves the answer for next time.
lines.cap: A [hit]: about [1 ms]. A [miss]: read the database, [save] it.
lines.heard: A hit comes back in about one millisecond. A miss reads the database, then saves the answer for next time.

lines.say: On a write, the app updates the database and deletes the cached copy, so nobody reads stale data.
lines.cap: On a write: update the database, [delete] the cached copy.
lines.heard: On a right, the app updates the database and deletes the cached copy, so nobody reads stale data.

lines.say: The queue is for work that shouldn't make the client wait. Like sending a confirmation email.
lines.cap: The [queue] is for work the client shouldn't [wait] for.
lines.heard: The queue is for work that shouldn't make the client wait, like sending a confirmation email.

lines.say: The API validates the request, drops a job on the queue, and answers right away.
lines.cap: Validate, [enqueue], answer [right away].
lines.heard: The API validates the request, drops a job on the queue, and answers right away.

lines.say: Workers do the slow part later. If a worker crashes, the job goes back on the queue.
lines.cap: [Workers] do the slow part. A crash? The job [goes back].
lines.heard: Workers do the slow part later. If a worker crashes, the job goes back on the queue.

lines.say: That buys you decoupling, durability, and a steady pace when traffic spikes.
lines.cap: [Decoupling], [durability], steady pace in a [spike].
lines.heard: that buys you decoupling durability and a steady pace when traffic spikes.

lines.say: The AI gateway is one front door for every model call. Your apps never talk to a provider directly.
lines.cap: The [AI gateway]: one front door for [every] model call.
lines.heard: The AI Gateway is one front door for every model call. Your apps never talk to a provider directly.

lines.say: It handles authentication, rate limits, caching, routing and cost tracking once, for everyone. And if a provider is down, it falls back to another.
lines.cap: [Auth], [limits], [caching], [routing], [cost]. A provider down? [Fallback].
lines.heard: It handles authentication, rate limits, caching, routing, and cost tracking once for everyone. And if a provider is down, it falls back to another.

lines.say: Request one, a simple read: GET slash products slash nine. It hits the C D N first.
lines.cap: Request one: [GET /products/9]. It hits the [CDN] first.
lines.heard: Request 1 a simple read, get slash product slash 9. It hits the CDN first.

lines.say: If the C D N has the answer cached, it returns right there. Nothing behind it ever hears about the request.
lines.cap: [Cached] at the edge? Done. Nothing behind it [hears] about it.
lines.heard: If the CDN has the answer cached, it returns right there. Nothing behind it ever hears about the request.

lines.say: If not, the gateway authenticates and rate limits, then routes it to the application service.
lines.cap: Not cached: the [gateway] checks, then [routes] to the app.
lines.heard: If not, the gateway authenticates and rate limits, then routes it to the application service.

lines.say: The app checks its cache. A hit skips the database. A miss queries it, then stores the result.
lines.cap: [Hit]: skip the database. [Miss]: query, then [store].
lines.heard: The app checks its cache, a hit skips the database, a misqueer is it, then stores the result.

lines.say: Then the response retraces the same path, back to the client.
lines.cap: The response [retraces] the same path back.
lines.heard: Then the response retraces the same path back to the client.

lines.say: Request two, a write: POST slash orders. This is the handbook's end to end view of it.
lines.cap: Request two: [POST /orders]. The [end to end] view.
lines.heard: Request to a right post slash orders. This is the handbook's end to end view of it.

lines.say: A POST isn't cached, so it passes straight through to the application service.
lines.cap: A POST is [not cached]: it passes [straight through].
lines.heard: A post isn't cached, so it passes straight through to the application service.

lines.say: The order service validates the body, commits to Post gress Q L in one transaction, updates Red iss, and publishes a message to the queue.
lines.cap: [Validate], [commit], update [Redis], [publish] a message.
lines.heard: The order service validates the body, commits to post -gress QL in one transaction, updates Redis and publishes a message to the queue.

lines.say: A two hundred one comes back in roughly twenty to one hundred fifty milliseconds. The worker sends the email after the response, so the client never waits.
lines.cap: [201] in about [20 to 150 ms]. The email goes out [after].
lines.heard: A 201 comes back in roughly 20 to 150 milliseconds. The worker sends the email after the response, so the client never waits.

lines.say: Request three, an AI chat message. The handbook traces it in seven steps.
lines.cap: Request three: [POST /chat]. Seven [steps].
lines.heard: Request 3, an AI chat message. The Handbook traces it in 7 steps.

lines.say: The gateway validates the token and checks the rate limit. The app loads the conversation from Post gress Q L, and checks Red iss.
lines.cap: [Gateway]: token, rate limit. [App]: Postgres, Redis.
lines.heard: The Gateway validates the token and checks the rate limit. The app loads the conversation from PostgreSQL and checks Redis.

lines.cap: The [AI gateway] routes to a provider, with a [fallback].
lines.heard: Then the app calls the AI Gateway, which routes to an available provider, with a fallback if the primary is down.

lines.cap: The answer [streams] back, token by token.
lines.heard: The answer streams back token by token through the app and the gateway to the client.

lines.say: And logging and cost tracking happen afterwards, through a queue, so they never slow the reply.
lines.cap: [Logging] and [cost] go through a [queue], after.
lines.heard: and logging and cost tracking happen afterwards through a queue, so they never slow the reply.

lines.say: Same map, three different paths. A read can stop at the C D N. A write goes to the database and queues the slow work. A chat goes through the AI gateway.

lines.heard: Same map, three different paths. A read can stop at the CDN. A write goes to the database and cues the slow work. A chat goes through the AI gateway. A chat goes through the AI gateway.

lines.cap: The handbook's [LLM gateway] example: a small [FastAPI] app.

lines.say: Now the most important rule. Not every API needs every layer. A small internal tool can be one application service with a database behind it, and that's the right architecture at that scale.
lines.cap: Not every API needs [every] layer. A small tool: [app] plus database. That's [right].
lines.heard: Now the most important rule. Not every API needs every layer. A small internal tool can be one application service with a database behind it, and that's the right architecture at that scale.

lines.say: Each layer buys you something. A cache buys latency. A gateway buys central auth. A queue buys resilience. But the price is more moving parts, more failure modes, more to operate.
lines.cap: [Cache]: latency. [Gateway]: central auth. [Queue]: resilience. The [price]: complexity.
lines.heard: Each layer buys you something. A cash buys latency. A gateway buys central auth. A queue buys resilience. But the price is more moving parts, more failure modes, more to operate.

lines.say: Mistake one. Assuming every API needs a gateway, a queue, and a cache from day one. Most don't, at first. Add a layer for a real problem, not a hypothetical one.
lines.cap: Mistake 1: every layer on [day one]. Add one for a [real] problem.
lines.heard: Mistake one. Assuming every API needs a gateway, a queue, and a cache from day one. Most don't at first. Add a layer for a real problem, not a hypothetical one.

lines.say: Mistake two. Treating microservices as automatically more production grade than a well built monolith. It depends on the problem. Part eleven covers it.
lines.cap: Mistake 2: [microservices] are not [automatically] better.
lines.heard: Mistake 2. Treating microservices as automatically more production grade than a well -built monolith. It depends on the problem. Part 11 covers it.

lines.say: Mistake three. Bolting the AI layer on as an afterthought. It needs its own timeouts, fallbacks, and cost tracking.
lines.cap: Mistake 3: AI as an [afterthought]. It needs [timeouts], [fallbacks], [cost] tracking.
lines.heard: Mistake 3. Bolting the AI layer on as an afterthought. It needs its own timeouts, fallbacks, and cost tracking.

lines.say: A database query is usually fast and predictable. A model call can be slow, non-deterministic, and billed by usage. That's why it deserves its own box.
lines.cap: A query is usually [fast]. A model call is [slow], [random], [metered].
lines.heard: A database query is usually fast and predictable. A model call can be slow, non -deterministic, and billed by usage. That's why it deserves its own box.
